sections.title: Wild radish
sections.text: Wild radish is an annual or biennial herb native from Europe through the Mediterranean to Central Asia. It may grow to about 1 m. The deeply lobed lower leaves, pale yellow four-petalled flowers and segmented pod shown here fit the species.

sections.title: Pods and food
sections.text: Kew records this species as used for food but does not specify which parts. Do not assume that every wild plant has the edible, developed storage root of cultivated radish; the related cultivated subspecies is treated separately in food references. ASPCA lists wild radish as toxic to horses. Human-safe parts and preparation were not verified here.

sections.title: Seeds
sections.text: The fruit is a segmented pod that remains closed at maturity, with one seed in each fertile segment; the plate's narrow, bead-like pod is a good match.
